description:
## Problem
On #4322 the `ci-paths` step greps `.ci-paths/changed.txt`, which `scripts/path_filter_decision.py` builds with rename detection on. A gated file that is renamed and edited in one pull request appears only under its new name, the filter does not match, the job is skipped and `core` accepts the skip. Reproduced on a scratch repository by renaming `tpcdi/scaling.py` and multiplying a row constant. The gate itself uses `--no-renames`, so the two sides compute different lists. `test_every_gated_generator_path_exists_or_is_a_documented_pattern` checks only the first pattern of each entry, so a renamed-away path silently leaves the table.

## Change
Make the generator-volume flag read a changed-file list built with `--no-renames` (old and new names), and make the existence test cover every pattern of every entry.

## Decision gates
Do not change what other flags in `ci-paths` read without checking each consumer.

## Verification rubric
Pass: a test builds a repository where a gated file is renamed and edited and asserts the flag is true; deleting or renaming any gated path fails the existence test; the two-way filter equality test still passes.

## Additions from the item review
- Precedent in the same CI step: `trunk-lane-changed.txt` is already built with `--no-renames`.

## Guardrails
- Any limit, default, threshold or label id or text is shown to the owner before it is committed. Briefs quote owner answers verbatim; questions to the owner carry no preselected answer.
- The implementer replies on review threads and leaves resolving them to the reviewer or the owner, unless the owner says otherwise (AGENTS.md asks agents to resolve benchbox-oracle threads on soundness paths; the owner has been asked which applies).
- Hosted writes (merge, close, disable or enable auto-merge, workflow dispatch, remote branch delete) only as the repository's close-out procedure or the owner's word for that pull request allows; never raw `gh pr merge` in core.
- No polling loop around `make pr-arm`, no `--no-verify`, no stand-in review unless the owner names the PR and head unprompted. Push only after `make pr-preflight` exits 0 on the exact head.
- No worktree takeover while another session may be working; no tracker write from a server that reports a stale version; never chain `git stash` with `git stash pop`.
- Heavy work runs only through `make heavy-run` or a lock-taking entry point, one run at a time.
- Status reports state only what merged and what was verified, with the evidence.
